source: Water evaporates when heated. Water vapor condenses when cooled. Precipitation returns water to the ground. Water collects in rivers and lakes.

board.title: The Waterworks Board
board.mission: Connect the waterworks and build two useful projects. Choose your route and collect evidence about temperature and the water cycle.
board.debrief: The completed waterworks connects temperature changes with the cycle that returns water to rivers and lakes.

locations.name: Heating station
locations.scene: A station for investigating the water cycle.
locations.instruction: What happens when liquid water is heated enough to become water vapor?
locations.explanation: Heating produces water vapor through evaporation; cooling vapor produces droplets through condensation.
locations.sourceQuote: Water evaporates when heated. Water vapor condenses when cooled. Precipitation returns water to the ground. Water collects in rivers and lakes.
hints: Connect the temperature change or event to its water-cycle process.
